name: Observation of the Higgs boson decay to a pair of tau leptons

significance.quote: the observed (expected) significance amounts to 6.4 (5.4) standard deviations
significance.value: 6.4σ observed (5.4σ expected), 13 TeV data combined with 7 and 8 TeV data

summary.plain: ATLAS reports an observation of the Higgs boson decaying into a pair of tau leptons (heavier cousins of the electron), from 13 TeV data combined with earlier 7 and 8 TeV data. The paper reports cross-section measurements, all in agreement with Standard Model expectations.
summary.technical: 36.1 fb⁻¹ of 13 TeV data: H → ττ signal established with observed (expected) significance 4.4 (4.1) standard deviations; combined with 7 and 8 TeV data, 6.4 (5.4) standard deviations, which 'constitutes an observation of H → ττ decays'. Total H → ττ cross section at 13 TeV 3.77 +0.60/−0.59 (stat) +0.87/−0.74 (syst) pb; all measurements in agreement with Standard Model expectations.

title: Cross-section measurements of the Higgs boson decaying into a pair of tau-leptons in proton-proton collisions at sqrt(s)=13 TeV with the ATLAS detector
why_it_matters: Tau leptons are heavier cousins of the electron, so this decay tests how the Higgs boson couples to leptons. The paper states that the combined significance constitutes an observation of H → ττ decays by the ATLAS experiment, with all measurements in agreement with Standard Model expectations.
